concerns.message: The new rule contradicts an existing test that the constraints say to keep. `simulation.test.ts:498` ("does not moor across a corner of land the hull could not sail past") puts the ship on the diagonal neighbour (dock.tileX-1, dock.tileY+1). It then asserts `sail(harbour, diagonal, INTERACT)` does not moor. Acceptance 1 now requires that exact case to moor. But the constraints say "keep ... every existing test, except the sweep this task rewrites".
concerns.consequence: The worker cannot meet acceptance 1 and the keep-every-test constraint together. It will either stop with a `question`, or quietly rewrite a test it was told to keep, and a reviewer may block the run for that. Settle it now: allow flipping the first half of that test (the diagonal case now moors) and keep its shoal-segment `hullPathIsClear` assertions.

concerns.message: The required negative test can't exist with the real tuning. Tiles are 256 sub-units and the reach is 384, so the 3×3 neighbourhood spans [centre-384, centre+384) on each axis. It therefore contains the whole reach disc except two points, (centre.x+384, centre.y) and (centre.x, centre.y+384). At both points the hull already covers the tiles between it and the berth, so the path is clear. So no position is "within 384 of a berth, separated by land, and not adjacent". In production the new rule means "any ship within reach moors". The hull-path check in `dockInReach` stops doing anything, and "a berth behind land doesn't moor" never applies.
concerns.consequence: The second test in acceptance 1 can't be written against the shipped `dockRadius`/tile size. The worker will burn time or ask a `question`. If it bends the test to fit, `docs/architecture.md` (acceptance 4) ends up describing a behind-land rule that never happens in the game. Settle it now: allow the negative test to use `testConfig(rows, { dockRadius: 640 })` (the helper already takes ship overrides; the shipped 384 is unchanged). Also accept that the doc can simply say "on or beside the berth tile, or within reach with a clear run".

concerns.message: The diagonal-neighbour rule has no guard against diagonal pinches. Say a diagonal neighbour is navigable, but both tiles it shares with the berth are land or shoal. Then the ship is in water the hull can't sail into the berth from, since a 160-wide hull can't pass through a corner point. Mooring would still snap it to the berth, and casting off puts it on the other side of the seam. Map validation only checks that the dock has orthogonal sea and land beside it, so nothing rules this layout out.
concerns.consequence: A future map (or a shoal placed near a dock) could let a ship cross a land or shoal barrier by mooring and casting off. Cheap fix: for a diagonal neighbour, require at least one of the two tiles it shares with the berth to be navigable. The review's head-on case still moors, because (dock.x, dock.y+1) is sea.

concerns.message: The adjacency rule has to live inside `dockInReach`, not as a separate check in `sail`. `apps/web/src/hud.ts:37` derives the "Press E to dock" hint from `dockInReach`. The corner-approach test at `simulation.test.ts:586-587` asserts `dockInReach(...) === corner` on the step that moors. Integration tests call it too.
concerns.consequence: If adjacency is added beside `dockInReach`, the HUD shows no hint in exactly the head-on spot this feature fixes. The existing real-map corner test also fails, because ships in column tx+1 now moor one step earlier through adjacency, while `dockInReach` is still undefined there.

concerns.message: Under the new rule, the sweep's outcome B can't fail. The reach sits inside the neighbourhood, and with E held every step inside the neighbourhood moors. So a lane that never moors can't have grounded within reach. The assertion looks strict but can never catch anything while the rule holds.
concerns.consequence: The rewritten sweep could let a later change slip through, for example one that shrinks the neighbourhood or regresses the snap. Make it bite: pin the exact set (or exact count per heading and speed) of lanes classified as B, named in the test, so any lane that changes class fails.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: Add one predicate inside `dockInReach`: return the nearest dock whose tile is the ship's tile or one of its 8 neighbours, with a diagonal-pinch guard (at least one of the two tiles the diagonal shares with the berth is navigable). Keep the existing reach-plus-clear-path branch as the fallback. At 256-sub-unit tiles and 384 reach, the neighbourhood already covers the reach disc, so this is the whole behaviour change. The HUD, the integration tests and the existing corner test then pick it up with no other code change. Flip only the diagonal half of the test at line 498, and build the negative 'behind land' test in a `testConfig` with a larger `dockRadius`.
structured_output.cheap_experiment: A throwaway vitest on the `harbour` config (no product change) takes about 10 minutes. First, enumerate every hull-clear sub-unit position within 384 of the berth centre and count how many lie outside the berth's 3×3 tile block. Expect exactly 2, both with a clear path. That settles whether acceptance 1's negative test is possible with the real tuning. Second, remove the `continue` at line 638 and patch `dockInReach` locally with the adjacency OR, then log each lane's class for headings 24–56 × 3 speeds × offsets. This confirms every lane moors or misses before the worker commits to a sweep design and exact counts.
